transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My sleep has been all over the place for weeks, and I can’t seem to get any real rest no matter how exhausted I feel. I'm just constantly worn out, and nothing I do seems to help me get a decent night's sleep.
Do you find it difficult to fall or stay asleep at night, or do you feel an uncontrollable urge to nap or fall asleep during the day despite having slept at night?

Yes, falling and staying asleep is a major struggle because I lie awake for hours listening to my husband's breathing or waking up every hour to check his monitor. When I do get some sleep, I wake up feeling like I've been hit by a truck instead of actually rested. I don't really have an urge to nap during the day, but I just carry this constant, heavy exhaustion with me.
Beyond your exhaustion, have you noticed a persistent loss of interest in activities you usually enjoy or a general feeling of sadness or hopelessness lately?

Yes, it feels like someone turned the color down on my whole life, and there's this heavy, hollow sadness in my chest that I just can't shake. I've also completely stopped doing my gardening and Saturday bird walks because even the thought of picking up my binoculars feels completely pointless now.
Besides the loss of interest in your hobbies, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite, your ability to concentrate, or have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living?

My appetite is completely gone, and I often realize it's mid-afternoon and I've had nothing but coffee, while my concentration is so shot that I'm making uncharacteristic errors with radiographs at work. Honestly, on my worst days, I've caught myself thinking it would be easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up tomorrow. It really scares me to admit that, but those thoughts have started creeping in.

To better understand the severity of what you are experiencing, could you tell me if you have been able to continue going to your job and performing your daily responsibilities, even if it is very difficult?

I am barely hanging on, and I've actually received formal write-ups at the clinic because of my mistakes on the radiographs. At home, everything is falling apart too—I'm neglecting basic chores, skipping my own doctor appointments, and constantly struggling to keep up with my husband's care. I feel so ashamed because I just can't manage any of it anymore.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have become noticeably slower, or conversely, that you feel an intense, restless agitation that makes it impossible for you to sit still?

No, I haven't really noticed my speech or movements becoming slower, and I don't feel that kind of intense physical restlessness either. I'm just incredibly exhausted and feel too heavy and drained to do much of anything.

Given the severity of the symptoms you've described, are you currently able to function at all in your daily life, or would you say that you are completely unable to perform even basic tasks or maintain your personal hygiene?

I'm not completely incapacitated, but I am barely functioning and struggling immensely. I've been neglecting basic household chores, skipping my own medical appointments, and facing write-ups at work for my mistakes. Almost all of my remaining energy is desperately channeled into keeping up with my husband's care, which leaves me too exhausted to maintain any of my normal routine.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a constellation of symptoms consistent with a major depressive episode of severe intensity, including persistent sadness, anhedonia, significant appetite loss, concentration deficits, sleep disturbance, and passive suicidal ideation. The severity is marked by significant functional impairment, including professional disciplinary action and neglect of personal health, without evidence of psychotic symptoms.
